subject.title: fix(agents): bound compaction planning worker payloads

question: Should OpenClaw adopt positional index restoration as the compaction worker fidelity contract while leaving history-prune planning full-fidelity?
rationale: The patch appears correct and well-proven, but this choice defines a session-state invariant across worker structured cloning and accepts one intentionally unbounded operation; repository history does not establish that product/runtime tradeoff without an agents-runtime owner.

options.title: Accept the indexed contract
options.body: Refresh onto current main, rerun the focused Worker fidelity proof, and land with the existing validated index restoration and documented history-prune exception.

options.title: Require stronger identity
options.body: Replace positional restoration with an explicit stable per-message planning identity before merge, accepting additional implementation complexity.

options.title: Pause for complete bounding
options.body: Hold the PR until history-prune can also return a bounded plan or deterministic repair operations rather than full message bodies.

recommendation.title: Accept the indexed contract
recommendation.body: Refresh onto current main, rerun the focused Worker fidelity proof, and land with the existing validated index restoration and documented history-prune exception.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the worker-backed planning architecture and are best positioned to judge its message-identity and history-prune contracts.
